zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 假日債市簡報

美國固定收益市場依美國證券業暨金融市場協會（SIFMA）的全天休市建議，於感恩節休市，當日沒有新的美國債券價格可供觀察。本日政策焦點在南韓：半導體景氣強勁，央行大幅上修經濟成長預測，並重啟升息。在其通膨評估中，半導體熱潮的影響仍大於家庭需求疲弱。

南韓央行升息25個基點至3.25%，最新預測也顯示仍有再升息空間。歐洲方面，歐洲央行10月會議紀錄顯示，官員雖同意採漸進步調，卻曾廣泛討論當次就升息的可能性。歐洲領袖並同意推薦Pablo Hernandez de Cos出任下一任歐洲央行總裁，推進領導層交接；屆時大幅改組的執行理事會將面對通膨居高不下與主權債務壓力。

## 全球利率、信用與主權動態

南韓央行在10月暫停升息後，以5票對2票決議升息，今年累計緊縮75個基點。彭博訪調的23位經濟學家中，有21位預期此次升息。更大的變化來自經濟展望：央行將2026年與2027年成長預測，由8月的3.3%與2.9%，分別上修至3.9%與4.1%；涵蓋12月至5月的未來六個月利率預測中位數，也由3.25%升至3.5%。

總裁申鉉松表示，及早採取預防性行動，可減少日後所需的緊縮幅度。央行將2027年通膨預測由2.3%上修至2.4%，今年預測維持2.7%，目前預期消費者物價通膨要到2028年才會收斂至2%目標。大信證券策略師Kong Dongrak認為，半導體產業在經濟中的比重上升，意味升息循環可能比先前預期更長，利率高點也更高。新榮證券的Cho Yong-gu則重新評估，下次升息是否可能由原先預期的4月提前至2月。

申鉉松也承認，晶片熱潮尚未明顯帶動家庭消費。他估計，今年半導體公司的營業利益接近700兆韓元，超過國民所得的五分之一，且所得流向企業利潤、而非薪資的比重異常偏高。他認為，這些收益終將透過稅收、獎金、股利及投資傳導至整體經濟。彭博經濟研究預期，央行將在2月進一步升息至3.5%，但全球AI投資放緩可能使這項預測落空。

歐洲央行會議紀錄進一步說明了10月維持利率不變的決策考量。許多委員表示，9月以來取得的資訊，已足以支持在該次會議升息。官員普遍認為通膨展望惡化，部分人士擔心通膨要到2028年之後才會回到目標。不過，他們仍判斷，這場主要由能源帶動的衝擊需要有節制的回應，目前證據尚不足以支持加快緊縮。

這份審慎態度有其具體依據。紀錄指出，迄今未出現顯著的第二輪效應；放款利率上升、貸款需求放緩，也顯示先前升息正順利傳導。短期成長展望轉差，委員並質疑AI投資與庫存累積還能支撐全球經濟多久。會議紀錄既呈現了進一步緊縮獲得廣泛支持，也交代了官員未採更強力措施的理由。

據知悉週四機密討論的人士透露，拉加德另向歐洲領袖表示，AI正協助歐洲抵禦能源成本上升。她將AI、能源與全球長期利率攀升，列為左右經濟展望的重要力量。她認為，政府與企業大規模發債，是長期利率上升的主要原因，市場預期央行將進一步提高借款成本，也推升了長期利率。

繼先前獲法德支持後，De Cos再獲歐盟領袖推薦，接班進程向前推進。歐洲理事會主席Antonio Costa表示，正式程序應於12月完成。De Cos仍須出席歐洲議會聽證，議會意見不具約束力；拉加德將於2月7日離任，之後由他接任。De Cos曾任西班牙央行總裁，現為國際清算銀行總經理，外界認為他較另一位候選人Klaas Knot偏鴿，但他也主張財政紀律，並警惕能源相關通膨。

這項人事協議還包括，由Laurence Boone在Isabel Schnabel於1月離任後接掌市場業務，以及由Markus Brunnermeier接替5月任期屆滿的首席經濟學家Philip Lane。因此，在Brunnermeier於6月就任前，德國將有五個月沒有執行理事會席次。若法國財政壓力妨礙貨幣政策傳導，主管市場業務的職位可能格外重要。法國興業銀行首席經濟學家Michala Marcussen表示，新任總裁將對歐洲央行政策工具的發展方向發揮重要作用，同時強調決策仍由集體作成。

日本央行審議委員田村直樹呼籲及早行動，將政策利率由目前的1.25%，推向他估計約2%的中性水準。他認為通膨尚未穩定錨定在2%目標，若向上偏離，可能需要加快升息。田村長期立場偏鷹，他表示，日本經濟仍將維持韌性，央行會持續觀察中東局勢、AI相關需求與匯率。

日本央行半年報則提供了另一項與財政有關的進展。截至9月底，央行持有的ETF市值為113.1兆日圓，其中未實現利益達76兆日圓，較六個月前增加33%。半年ETF收益達2兆日圓，主要來自出售及股利。首相高市早苗希望以出售獲利支應國家安全政策；能否繳庫及繳庫金額，取決於央行在3月底年度結束後的淨收益計算。

最新披露的利益，讓這項構想背後的資產規模更為明確。央行上月決定，將按帳面價值計算的每年出售額由3,300億日圓提高至8,600億日圓，但估計仍需43年才能出清持有部位。前審議委員櫻井真曾建議加快出售，以緩解政府籌資壓力，以及政治上對升息的阻力。總裁植田和男上週表示，出售決定是由日本央行獨立作成。

加拿大六大銀行目前全數預測12月升息，TD是最後一家提前升息預測的銀行；CIBC與BMO已在本週稍早將預期時點由1月提前。加拿大央行總裁Tiff Macklem先前警告，能源成本可能延後轉嫁，TD經濟學家Andrew Hencic因而將可能的升息解讀為管理通膨風險。BMO的Benjamin Reitzes表示，總裁談話並未清楚暗示再升息一次後就會暫停。

盧安達則立即採取更大幅度的緊縮，央行將基準利率由8.75%升至9.5%，連續第四次升息，達至少2009年以來最高水準；商業銀行存款準備率也由5%提高至7%。食品供應減少推升價格，都市地區通膨由1月的8.9%升至10月的19.5%。總裁Soraya Hakuziyaremye表示，目標是讓通膨回到5%。降雨不足已衝擊農業，預期中的聖嬰天氣型態可能造成進一步干擾。

英國央行《金融穩定報告》針對主權債市風險，提出加強管控英國公債附買回交易槓桿的方向。央行正考慮對未經集中結算的交易設定最低擔保品折扣率，並擴大集中結算，預定於2027年上半年提出改革路線圖。目前大部分英國公債附買回交易不設折扣，價值100英鎊的擔保品即可借得100英鎊，對擔保品跌價沒有初始緩衝。

央行發現，交易商之間的競爭使融資條件偏寬鬆，卻未搭配充分的淨額結算或投資組合保證金保障。部分較小型銀行對所有英國公債附買回交易均採零折扣。交易商對主要非銀行機構的現金淨放款，自2023年以來約增加一倍，由£1,000億增至£2,000億。最低折扣率將減少以英國公債作擔保所能取得的現金，並可能限制槓桿。

央行也指出9月與10月的一條跨境傳導管道：部分避險基金集中持有法國主權債的部位虧損後，減持其他主權債，並縮減英國公債附買回交易部位。即使已部分降槓桿，避險基金在法國主權債的整體槓桿仍偏高。央行估計，擴大集中結算，可使正常情況下的中介承作能力增加最多£190億，壓力期間增加£240億。Managed Funds Association支持擴大自願性集中結算與強化基礎設施，並強調避險基金對債市流動性的貢獻。英國央行另提出措施，將使英國銀行的資本要求再降低30個基點。

洲際交易所（ICE）則作出直接影響英國公債市場部位的決定。在週四收盤後發布的通知中，ICE撤回一項提案：原擬將旗下主力、約10年期的英國公債期貨可交割券，限於原始發行期限不超過16年的債券。原先以更長期限發行的舊券，將繼續保有交割資格。Lloyds分析師先前指出，投資人為規則變更預作準備，已使這些債券相對於提案下仍具交割資格的債券變得便宜。

原提案旨在處理交割券愈來愈集中於低票息債券的問題。低票息債券的稅務待遇影響相對評價，英國央行大量持有相關債券，也可能影響流動性。保留現行規則，意味這些特徵仍將存在；恢復交易時，先前的相對價值調整也可能回轉。

彭博關於德國資產交換交易的報導，呈現另一項主權風險部位的變化。投資人愈來愈常將德國公債與交換合約搭配，降低單純的利率曝險，將交易焦點放在德國公債相對衍生工具的表現。花旗的Fabio Lisanti表示，這類保護需求正在增加；德國商業銀行的Hauke Siemssen則指出，10月法國財政動盪期間，2年期德國資產交換交易表現強勁。

德國自2025年起為國防與基礎建設增加發債，使德國公債相對交換合約變便宜，改善了這筆交易的進場條件。其避險效果有賴壓力期間德國公債優於交換合約的表現。StoneX的Shriya Samarth另指出，年底資產負債表限制，以及市場對短天期現金工具的需求，也使以衍生工具管理利率曝險更具吸引力。受限而不能使用衍生工具，或希望直接持有未避險債券利率部位的投資人，所面對的限制則不同。

問題企業債方面，知情人士向彭博透露，萬科正討論將12月15日到期的人民幣12億元本金展延三年，3%票息則按時支付。目前與債權人討論的各項方案，前期本金償還比例均不到過往40%的一半。條件仍可協商，最快週五可能向更多債權人提出。

若採取較低的前期現金償付，債權人取得的展延誘因將不如以往。萬科1月曾同意先償還40%的本金，換得一年展延；最新季度虧損人民幣89.9億元，合約銷售額年減48.3%。這次協商之際，珠海華發先前未能按時支付兩項信託產品款項，並尋求銀行貸款展延，再度引發市場對具國企背景地產企業能獲多少支持的疑慮。華發之後已償還相關信託債務。

農產品貿易商Trans-Oil年報披露，一筆出口前融資仍有尚未解決的財務承諾條款違約，增添其流動性的不確定性。公司預期在11月30日前取得豁免，但表示無法保證；另兩筆融資已取得豁免。尚未解決的違約，是使公司持續經營能力存在重大不確定性的因素之一。

截至6月30日，Trans-Oil未達兩項要求：EBITDA須至少為淨財務費用的1.75倍，以及調整後淨負債不得超過EBITDA的3倍。該筆融資帳面價值約$1.33億，標普所列總規模為$2.47億。年度財務成本由$1.093億增至$1.679億，原先$5,390萬的獲利轉為$4,580萬虧損，其中包含仲裁相關準備$1,930萬。公司將流動性吃緊的部分原因歸於黑海航運與保險成本上升，以及多瑙河水位偏低。Trans-Oil另已要求延後支付$7.5億債券的票息，並與重整顧問合作，這次豁免協商也是更廣泛融資檢討的一環。

德國一項上訴判決，強化了依據英國程序重整柏林Project Fuerst的貸款銀行地位。法蘭克福法院推翻下級法院有利於KVH的裁決；KVH原要求全額償還一筆€500萬貸款，該貸款在2024年倫敦重整中遭展延，償付順位也被調降。上訴法院認定，英國《公司法》Part 26A程序與德國相應程序在結構上相似，應予承認。法院也駁回KVH其後終止修訂後貸款的主張，認為欠缺理由及契約要求的足額同意。KVH仍可向德國聯邦最高法院上訴；這起攸關英國脫歐後跨境執行的案件，仍可能接受進一步司法審查。

收購融資方面，貸款機構持續安排大額新承諾。由Nordic Capital、加拿大退休金計畫投資委員會（CPPIB）與安大略教師退休金計畫等組成的財團收購Cary Group，Ares將提供約130億瑞典克朗、即$13億的單一分層融資（unitranche），將優先順位與次順位貸款整合於同一安排。知悉融資的人士表示，貸款規模約為Cary近20億瑞典克朗EBITDA的6.5倍；該EBITDA採IFRS調整後口徑，不計租賃成本。Ares原已是貸款人，計畫自行持有整筆融資。

這筆交易對該汽車擋風玻璃維修業者的估值超過€30億，CVC將全數退出投資。安大略教師退休金計畫與CPPIB預計分別投資€5.45億與€5億。交易預定於2027年上半年完成，仍須取得一般監管核准。

銀行也已為KKR收購包裝供應商Logoplaste安排€5.5億貸款，另計畫提供€1.5億循環額度。安排銀行包括巴克萊、桑坦德、荷蘭合作銀行、裕信銀行與高盛。Logoplaste約有等值€7.7億的定期貸款於2028年到期。此次收購估值可能超過€12億；相較之下，安大略教師退休金計畫在2021年收購60%股權時，估值為€14億。知悉出售事宜的人士表示，該退休金計畫將無法從這筆投資獲利。

印度Adani Enterprises與Adani Power正準備公開發債，總額至少200億盧比、即$2.2億。知情人士表示，兩家公司各可能募集100億至200億盧比，其中一筆目標在12月底前發行，另一筆在3月，條件尚未敲定。在截至3月的本會計年度，印度企業公開發債募資額已達484億盧比，前一完整年度則為1,134億盧比，顯示相較私募，這條融資管道規模仍有限。Crisil給予Adani Power的國內評等為AA+；Adani Enterprises獲ICRA升評後，目前評等為AA，展望穩定。

菲律賓則以一項規模較小、但形式不同的進展，擴大主權融資的投資人參與管道。PDAX執行長Nichel Gaba表示，本月約$13億的零售美元債發行中，約1,200位投資人以穩定幣出資，購買合計約$100萬債券。這批3年期債券票息為5.65%，最低投資額$200；Gaba表示，零售投資人平均購買額為$750。可接受的代幣包括USDC、USDT、USDPT與RLUSD，均在交割前轉換成美元。Gaba稱，這是首次接受主要穩定幣購買主權美元債，並認為未來有望觸及沒有銀行帳戶及旅居海外的菲律賓人。

市場看好菲律賓本幣債券的漲勢可延續至2027年，支持因素包括預期2027年上半年納入摩根大通新興市場指數、通膨下降與發行減少。Brandywine的Carol Lye於11月增持後，指出上述供需因素。週二3年期公債標售投標倍數達4.48倍，為2025年8月以來最高；相較之下，11月4日的7年期標售，原欲募集300億披索，最終僅募得155億披索。標售需求改善，讓未來可能的指數資金流入，也有本地需求作為呼應。

衣索比亞正式邀請持有其違約$10億債券的投資人，換入一檔新發行的$8.8億債券。換債要約至12月11日截止，預計12月18日前完成。新券於2029年7月到期，票息6.15%，並納入$9,900萬逾期利息及0.5%同意費。當局表示，臨時債權人委員會成員支持條件，並有意參與。

這項要約推進了6月議定、8月獲官方債權人批准的方案。條件包括一項新資金認購權憑證，讓投資人可依約定商業條件，認購未來發行的國際債券。若換債完成，將結束三年的違約狀態；此前的協商依G20共同框架進行，期間曾因債券持有人與官方債權人所提供的債務減免是否具可比性而出現爭議。

迦納完成提前贖回126億塞地、即$11億的重整後本幣債券，全數接受三天要約期間提交的債券，占該期未償餘額44%，另支付2.89億塞地應計利息。贖回較2027年2月到期日提前三個月，可降低未來利息成本，並向銀行與其他投資人釋出現金。財政部計畫兩週後就剩餘債券再度開放要約。

其他主權消息方面，標普暗示可能跟進穆迪調降波蘭評等。該國公共財政惡化，政府、總統、央行與憲法法院之間的衝突，也加深投資人疑慮。巴西方面，知情人士表示，總統魯拉曾探詢Bradesco董事長Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi加入政府的意願，可能職位包括財政部長。這項仍在考慮中的任命，使市場對財政政策方向抱持期待。

國際貨幣基金（IMF）一項研究計畫提供了更廣泛的財政比較。新推出的Global Fiscal Actions資料集，利用大型語言模型將142國自1990年以來的裁量性財政措施分類，並由研究人員抽樣查核。初步結果顯示，先進經濟體以外的政府支出措施，通常會強化景氣循環，但過去十年間，各類國家的這項傾向都有減弱。稅收措施與景氣循環的相關性則低得多。研究著眼於各國政府在不同歷史時期採取的政策行動，將政策選擇與通常用來評估財政的預算結果區分開來。

對於華府擬議的新關稅，各貿易夥伴的最新回應以協商為主。各國表達失望與反對，中國與歐盟並保留在美國超出既有協議時採取報復的可能。完成書面意見徵集與公開聽證後，關稅最快可能於1月下旬實施。新加坡反駁美國認定其政策助長製造業產能過剩的說法，表示將爭取重新考慮最高20%的關稅。

越南面臨擬議35%關稅，可能削弱其吸引製造商分散中國產能時所具備的部分優勢。東南亞去年吸引創紀錄的$2,460億外國直接投資。越南美國商會執行長Travis Mitchell表示，稅率不確定，增加了定價、銷售預測、生產及投資的難度。韓禮士基金會的Deborah Elms認為，相對稅率的變動可能促使部分企業重新考慮在中國生產，但既有工廠仍難以搬遷。印度擬議稅率為17%，若未達成貿易協議，可能升至25%，最終負擔仍高度取決於談判。

晶片限制則帶來更具體的融資阻礙。彭博報導，貝恩資本旗下Bridge Data Centres尋求增額至$66億的貸款，因額外盡職調查而延誤進度，其馬來西亞設施據稱服務字節跳動。《金融時報》另報導，美國收緊中國取得先進晶片的管道之際，輝達已要求AI硬體製造商停止向東南亞出貨伺服器。荷蘭反對美國擬對ASML施加的域外限制，認為將威脅該公司。設備能否取得及終端使用者合規要求，因而直接影響融資進度。

企業消息方面，SAP考慮在聚焦AI的重整中，裁減至少10,000個職位，相當於員工總數至少9%。知情人士表示，人數可能在勞資協商後變動；德國員工的就業保障承諾延續至2028年。日本菸草與奧馳亞則正研究收購Imperial Brands的可能性。Imperial Brands表示會考慮提案，但尚未接獲任何洽詢。

銀行交易與監管則帶來不同的資本議題。杜拜伊斯蘭銀行宣布以全換股方式收購Emirates Islamic，合併後集團資產約$1,590億。該行將向Emirates NBD發行34.9億股，對標的估值約311億迪拉姆、即$85億。瑞士國會委員會支持將瑞銀資本要求提高$160億後，瑞銀管理層出面安撫員工。裕信銀行計畫在收購取得最終監管核准後，提名Andrea Orcel擔任德國商業銀行監事會主席，並尋求更換全部10席股東代表。

## 下一交易日觀察

週五恢復交易後，英國公債市場將反映ICE的決定。期貨於倫敦時間凌晨1時開盤，早於上午8時的現券市場，投資人將首次有機會調整先前為交割券限制提案建立的部位。信用方面，萬科可能在週五向更多債權人傳閱展延條件；Trans-Oil預計11月30日前取得豁免，則是近期另一項融資期限。

中東局勢仍可能改變央行決策所依據的能源假設。胡塞武裝攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯紅海港口，據報吉贊受損輕微、沒有平民受傷，吉達伊斯蘭港附近則攔截一架無人機。沙國一座煉油廠也遭攻擊，威脅出口。伊朗聲稱荷姆茲海峽有船隻觸雷，尚未獲獨立證實。沙國主導的產油國聯盟正考慮將現行產量配額延續至1月。出口中斷與最終產量決定，都可能在債市恢復交易時改變通膨展望。

巴克萊經濟學家認為，西班牙11月29日大選對主權債的考驗相對有限，因為政府很可能由主流中間偏右或中間偏左政黨領導。Scope Ratings表示，該國信用展望仍獲得相對不受選舉週期影響的因素支持。企業政策可能出現較明顯變化：人民黨主張延長核能發電，並取消分階段實施、要求資料中心每小時用電需求的80%來自再生能源的規定。這些提議將改變公用事業與高耗電投資所面對的監管環境。

加拿大下週公布季度GDP與11月就業數據，時間早於12月9日利率決策，將檢驗六大銀行一致預測升息所依據的經濟韌性。菲律賓11月通膨將於12月4日公布，可直接檢驗支持本幣債券續漲預期的物價壓力緩和論點。聯準會H.4.1資產負債表報告因感恩節由週四順延，訂於紐約時間11月27日週五下午4時30分發布。

overall_summary.headline: 南韓升息，歐洲央行會議紀錄凸顯通膨風險未退
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場因感恩節休市，當日沒有新的美國債券價格可供觀察。南韓央行升息25個基點至3.25%，並將2026年與2027年成長預測分別上修至3.9%與4.1%，未來六個月利率預測中位數也升至3.5%。半導體利潤支撐較強的經濟展望，但效益尚未明顯擴散至家庭消費；全球AI投資若放緩，仍可能影響後續升息。

歐洲央行10月會議紀錄顯示，許多官員認為已有理由立即升息。不過，面對主要由能源帶動的衝擊，官員選擇漸進回應，考量是迄今未見顯著第二輪效應，且先前緊縮正透過銀行放款傳導。歐盟領袖推薦Pablo Hernandez de Cos出任下任總裁，正式程序預期12月完成；這次交接之際，通膨居高不下與主權債務壓力仍是政策挑戰。

英國央行考慮為英國公債附買回交易設定最低擔保品折扣率，以限制槓桿。ICE另撤回公債期貨交割券限制提案，先前受影響債券相對變便宜的走勢，可能在恢復交易後回轉。信用方面，萬科討論將人民幣12億元本金展延三年，前期還款條件不如過往交易；Trans-Oil預期11月30日前取得財務承諾條款豁免，但仍無把握。衣索比亞則啟動換債，擬以$8.8億新券置換違約的$10億債券。

英國公債週五恢復交易，將首度反映ICE的決定。中東攻擊事件與沙國主導產油國聯盟尚待決定的產量政策，可能在債市重開時，改變央行政策背後的能源假設。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Thanksgiving Day, in line with SIFMA's full-close recommendation, leaving no same-day U.S. bond price discovery. The leading policy development came from South Korea, where the central bank resumed tightening and sharply upgraded its growth forecasts as the semiconductor boom continued to outweigh weak household demand in its inflation assessment.

The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, with its updated projections pointing to room for another increase. In Europe, the ECB's October meeting account revealed how broadly officials had considered an immediate hike even while agreeing to proceed gradually. European leaders also agreed to recommend Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next ECB president, advancing a leadership transition that will place inflation persistence and sovereign-debt strains before a substantially reshaped Executive Board.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

The BOK's 5-2 decision followed an October pause and brought this year's tightening to 75 basis points. Twenty-one of 23 economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected the increase. The larger change was in the economic outlook: officials raised their growth forecasts to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027, from 3.3% and 2.9% in August. The median six-month rate projection rose to 3.5% from 3.25%, covering December through May.

Governor Shin Hyun Song said preemptive action could limit the amount of tightening required later. The bank raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 2.4% from 2.3%, left this year's at 2.7%, and now expects consumer-price inflation to converge to its 2% target only in 2028. Daishin Securities strategist Kong Dongrak said the semiconductor sector's growing economic weight suggested a longer tightening cycle and a higher peak than previously expected. Shinyoung Securities' Cho Yong-gu was reconsidering whether the next increase could come in February instead of April.

Shin acknowledged that the chip boom had yet to spread strongly into household consumption. He estimated semiconductor companies' operating profits at nearly 700 trillion won this year, more than a fifth of national income, with an unusually large share accruing to corporate profits rather than wages. Taxes, bonuses, dividends and investment would eventually transmit that income to the broader economy, he argued. Bloomberg Economics expects a further increase to 3.5% in February, while identifying a slowdown in global AI investment as a risk to that forecast.

The ECB account added an institutional explanation for October's decision to hold rates. A large number of members said the information available since September could have justified an increase at that meeting. Officials broadly agreed that the inflation outlook had worsened, and some worried that inflation would return to target only after 2028. They nevertheless judged that the predominantly energy-driven shock still called for a measured response and that evidence was insufficient to accelerate tightening.

That restraint reflected specific observations. The account recorded no material second-round effects so far, while higher lending rates and slowing loan demand indicated that earlier increases were transmitting smoothly. The near-term growth outlook had become gloomier, and members questioned how long AI investment and inventory accumulation could sustain global activity. The account therefore documented both the breadth of support for further restraint and the reasons officials had resisted a more forceful response.

Lagarde separately told European leaders that AI was helping the region withstand higher energy costs, according to people familiar with Thursday's confidential discussion. She identified AI, energy and rising global long-term interest rates as major forces shaping the outlook. In her assessment, large-scale government and corporate bond issuance was the main driver of the rise in long-term rates, with expectations of higher central-bank borrowing costs also contributing.

EU leaders' recommendation of De Cos moved the succession beyond the earlier Franco-German backing. Council President Antonio Costa said the formal process should finish in December. De Cos must still appear before the European Parliament, whose opinion is nonbinding, before succeeding Lagarde when she leaves on February 7. The former Bank of Spain governor and current Bank for International Settlements chief has been regarded as more dovish than rival candidate Klaas Knot, while advocating fiscal discipline and vigilance over energy-related inflation.

The agreement also encompasses Laurence Boone for the markets portfolio after Isabel Schnabel leaves in January, and Markus Brunnermeier to succeed chief economist Philip Lane when his term ends in May. Germany would consequently have no Executive Board seat for five months before Brunnermeier starts in June. The markets role could be particularly consequential if French fiscal strains interfere with monetary-policy transmission. Societe Generale chief economist Michala Marcussen said the incoming president would have an important role in shaping the direction of the ECB's policy toolkit, while emphasizing that decisions are collective.

In Japan, BOJ board member Naoki Tamura urged early action to bring the policy rate toward his estimate of a neutral level around 2%, compared with the current 1.25%. He argued that inflation was not firmly anchored at the 2% target and that upward deviations could require accelerated increases. Tamura, a longstanding hawk, said Japan's economy would remain resilient while the bank monitored Middle East developments, AI-related demand and exchange rates.

The BOJ's half-year accounts supplied a separate fiscal development. Its ETF holdings were worth 113.1 trillion yen at the end of September, including 76 trillion yen of unrealized gains, up 33% over six months. ETF income, mainly from sales and dividends, reached 2 trillion yen in the half-year. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wants sale profits to help fund her national-security agenda; transfers to the Treasury depend on the BOJ's annual net-income calculation after March-end.

The newly disclosed gains quantify the asset pool behind that proposal. Last month's decision to increase annual sales to 860 billion yen on a book-value basis, from 330 billion yen, would still take an estimated 43 years to dispose of the holdings. Former board member Makoto Sakurai has suggested faster sales could ease government funding pressures and political resistance to rate increases. Governor Kazuo Ueda said last week that the BOJ made the sale decision independently.

Canada's six largest banks now all forecast a December increase, with TD the last to bring its call forward. CIBC and BMO had shifted their expectations from January earlier in the week. TD economist Andrew Hencic characterized the prospective move as management of inflation risks after Governor Tiff Macklem's warnings about delayed energy-cost pass-through. BMO's Benjamin Reitzes said the governor's remarks offered no clear signal of a pause after another hike.

Rwanda delivered a larger immediate tightening. The central bank raised its key rate to 9.5% from 8.75%, its fourth consecutive increase and the highest level since at least 2009, and lifted commercial banks' required reserve ratio to 7% from 5%. Urban inflation reached 19.5% in October, compared with 8.9% in January, as reduced food supply pushed up prices. Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye said the objective was to restore inflation to 5%. Poor rainfall has hurt agriculture, with an expected El Nino weather pattern threatening further disruption.

Britain's Financial Stability Report set out a different response to sovereign-market risk: tighter control of leverage in gilt repo. The BOE is considering minimum haircuts on transactions outside central clearing, alongside broader use of clearing, with a reform roadmap due in the first half of 2027. Most gilt repo currently carries no haircut, allowing 100 pounds of borrowing against 100 pounds of collateral without an initial buffer for a fall in its value.

The bank found that competition among dealers had produced generous financing terms without adequate netting or portfolio-margining safeguards. Several smaller banks applied zero haircuts to every gilt repo transaction. Dealers' net cash lending to key nonbank institutions had roughly doubled since 2023, from 100 billion pounds to 200 billion pounds. Minimum haircuts would reduce the cash available against gilts and potentially constrain leverage.

The BOE also identified a cross-border transmission channel in September and October: losses on concentrated French sovereign positions prompted some hedge funds to cut other sovereign exposures and reduce gilt repo positions. Overall hedge-fund leverage in French sovereign debt remained elevated despite some deleveraging. Greater central clearing could add up to 19 billion pounds of intermediation capacity in normal conditions and 24 billion pounds under stress, the bank estimated. The Managed Funds Association supported expanded voluntary clearing and stronger infrastructure, stressing hedge funds' contribution to bond-market liquidity. Separately, the BOE outlined measures that would reduce UK lenders' capital requirements by another 30 basis points.

ICE made an immediate decision affecting gilt-market positioning. In a notice issued after Thursday's market close, it abandoned a proposal to restrict the delivery basket of its flagship roughly 10-year gilt futures contract to securities originally issued with maturities of 16 years or less. Older bonds issued at longer tenors will remain eligible. Lloyds analysts had reported that those bonds had cheapened relative to securities that would have remained eligible under the proposal as investors prepared for a rule change.

The proposed restriction had sought to address a basket increasingly concentrated in low-coupon bonds, whose tax treatment affects relative valuations and whose liquidity can also be influenced by large BOE holdings. Keeping the existing rules leaves those features intact and creates scope for the earlier relative-value adjustment to reverse when trading resumes.

A Bloomberg account of German asset swaps described another change in sovereign-risk positioning. Investors are increasingly combining Bund holdings with swaps to reduce outright interest-rate exposure and concentrate on Bund performance relative to derivatives. Citi's Fabio Lisanti described growing demand for that form of protection; Commerzbank's Hauke Siemssen highlighted strong performance by two-year German asset swaps during October's French fiscal turmoil.

Germany's increased issuance for defense and infrastructure since 2025 has made Bunds cheaper relative to swaps, improving the entry point for that trade. Its protection depends on Bunds outperforming swaps during stress. StoneX's Shriya Samarth also cited year-end balance-sheet constraints and demand for short-dated cash instruments as reasons derivatives become more attractive for managing rate exposure. Investors restricted from derivatives, or seeking unhedged duration, face different constraints.

In distressed corporate debt, Vanke is discussing a three-year extension of 1.2 billion yuan of principal due December 15 while paying the 3% coupon on time, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Possible upfront principal payments discussed with creditors were all less than half the 40% paid in previous extension deals. Terms remain negotiable and could be presented more widely as early as Friday.

The lower potential cash payment would mark a deterioration in creditor sweeteners. In January, Vanke secured a one-year extension after agreeing to repay 40% upfront. Its latest quarterly loss was 8.99 billion yuan and contracted sales fell 48.3% annually. The talks come amid renewed concern about support for state-linked property businesses after Zhuhai Huafa missed payments on two trust products and sought bank-loan extensions. Huafa has since repaid the trust debts.

Trans-Oil's annual accounts revealed an unresolved covenant breach on a pre-export facility, adding to uncertainty about the agricultural trader's liquidity. The company expects a waiver by November 30 but said it could not guarantee one. It has obtained waivers on two other facilities. The outstanding breach is among the factors creating material uncertainty over its ability to continue as a going concern.

As of June 30, Trans-Oil had breached requirements for EBITDA to cover net finance charges by at least 1.75 times and for adjusted net debt not to exceed 3 times EBITDA. The facility's carrying value was about $133 million; S&P puts its total size at $247 million. Annual finance costs rose to $167.9 million from $109.3 million, and a $53.9 million profit became a $45.8 million loss, including a $19.3 million arbitration-related provision. The firm attributes part of its liquidity squeeze to higher Black Sea shipping and insurance costs and low Danube water levels. Its request to defer coupons on $750 million of notes and work with restructuring advisers put the waiver negotiations alongside a broader financing review.

A German appeals ruling strengthened the position of lenders relying on a UK restructuring of Berlin's Project Fuerst. The Frankfurt court overturned a lower-court decision favoring KVH, which sought full repayment of a 5 million euro loan extended and subordinated in the project's 2024 London restructuring. The appeals court said Part 26A proceedings were structurally similar to Germany's corresponding process and should be recognized. It also rejected KVH's later attempt to terminate the amended loan for lack of grounds and a sufficient contractual quorum. KVH can appeal to Germany's Supreme Court, leaving further judicial review possible in a case important to cross-border enforcement after Brexit.

Acquisition lenders continued to arrange substantial new commitments. Ares is providing around 13 billion Swedish kronor, or $1.3 billion, of unitranche financing for Cary Group's buyout by a consortium including Nordic Capital, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and Ontario Teachers'. The debt combines senior and junior lending and represents about 6.5 times Cary's near-2 billion kronor of post-IFRS EBITDA, a measure excluding lease costs, according to people familiar with the financing. Existing lender Ares plans to retain the whole package.

The transaction values the windshield-repair business above 3 billion euros and would fully exit CVC's investment. Ontario Teachers' and CPPIB expect to invest 545 million euros and 500 million euros, respectively. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

Banks have also lined up 550 million euros of loans for KKR's acquisition of packaging supplier Logoplaste, with a further 150 million euro revolving facility planned. Arrangers include Barclays, Santander, Rabobank, UniCredit and Goldman Sachs. The company has about 770 million euros-equivalent of term loans due in 2028. The purchase could value Logoplaste above 1.2 billion euros, compared with 1.4 billion euros when Ontario Teachers' bought a 60% stake in 2021; people familiar with the sale said the pension plan would not realize a gain.

India's Adani Enterprises and Adani Power are preparing public bond offerings totaling at least 20 billion rupees, or $220 million. Each could raise 10 billion-20 billion rupees, with one sale targeted by December-end and the other in March, according to people familiar with the plans. Terms remain unsettled. Indian public corporate bond fundraising has reached 48.4 billion rupees in the fiscal year ending March, against 113.4 billion rupees in the preceding full year, illustrating the limited scale of this channel relative to private placements. Adani Power carries a domestic AA+ rating from Crisil; ICRA rates Adani Enterprises AA with a stable outlook after an upgrade.

The Philippines reported a smaller but distinct extension of sovereign funding access. About 1,200 investors used stablecoins to fund roughly $1 million of purchases in this month's approximately $1.3 billion retail dollar bond sale, according to PDAX chief executive Nichel Gaba. The three-year notes pay 5.65%, with a $200 minimum investment; Gaba put the average retail purchase at $750. Accepted tokens included USDC, USDT, USDPT and RLUSD, and were converted into dollars before settlement. Gaba described the transaction as the first acceptance of major stablecoins for purchases of sovereign dollar bonds and saw scope to reach unbanked and overseas Filipinos.

Domestic Philippine bonds have separately attracted expectations of further gains into 2027, supported by prospective JPMorgan emerging-market index inclusion in the first half, lower inflation and reduced issuance. Brandywine's Carol Lye cited those demand and supply factors after adding holdings in November. Tuesday's three-year auction drew 4.48 times coverage, the highest since August 2025, compared with a November 4 seven-year sale that raised only 15.5 billion pesos against a 30 billion peso target. The improvement in auction appetite gives the prospective index inflows a concrete domestic-demand counterpart.

Ethiopia formally invited holders of its defaulted $1 billion bond to exchange into a new $880 million security. The offer runs to December 11, with completion envisaged by December 18. The replacement matures in July 2029, carries a 6.15% coupon and includes $99 million of past-due interest and a 0.5% consent fee. The authorities said members of the ad hoc bondholder committee supported the terms and intended to participate.

The launch advances terms agreed in June and approved by official creditors in August. Those terms included a new-money warrant giving investors the right to subscribe to a future international bond on agreed commercial terms. The exchange would end a three-year default following negotiations under the G20 Common Framework and an earlier dispute over the comparability of relief with official creditors.

Ghana completed an early redemption of 12.6 billion cedis, or $1.1 billion, of restructured domestic bonds, accepting every security tendered during a three-day offer. That represented 44% of the outstanding issue, with another 289 million cedis paid in accrued interest. Redemption came three months before the February 2027 maturity, reducing future interest costs and releasing cash to banks and other investors. The Finance Ministry plans to reopen the offer for the remaining bonds in two weeks.

Elsewhere, S&P signaled it could follow Moody's in lowering Poland's rating as deteriorating public finances and conflict involving the government, presidency, central bank and Constitutional Court raised investor concerns. In Brazil, Lula sounded out Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi about joining the government, potentially as finance minister, according to people familiar with the discussions. The prospect drew hopes for fiscal-policy direction while the appointment remained under consideration.

An IMF research initiative offered a wider fiscal comparison. Its new Global Fiscal Actions dataset uses large language models to classify discretionary measures in 142 countries since 1990, with staff checking a sample. Initial findings showed spending actions tended to reinforce the economic cycle outside advanced economies, although that tendency had diminished across all country groups over the past decade. Tax measures were much less correlated with the cycle. The findings concern governments' actions across historical periods, distinguishing the policy choices from the budget outcomes usually used to assess them.

New responses to Washington's proposed tariffs centered on negotiation. Trading partners expressed disappointment and objections, while China and the EU preserved the possibility of retaliation if the U.S. exceeded existing agreements. Implementation could begin in late January after written comments and public hearings. Singapore disputed the U.S. finding that its policies contribute to excess manufacturing capacity and said it would seek reconsideration of tariffs of up to 20%.

Vietnam faces a proposed 35% levy, threatening part of the advantage that drew manufacturers diversifying from China. Southeast Asia received a record $246 billion of foreign direct investment last year. American Chamber of Commerce in Vietnam executive director Travis Mitchell said uncertainty over tariff rates complicated pricing, sales forecasts, production and investment. Hinrich Foundation's Deborah Elms argued that the changing relative rates could encourage some businesses to reconsider Chinese production, although moving established factories remains difficult. India's proposed 17% rate could rise to 25% without a trade agreement, keeping negotiations central to the final burden.

Chip restrictions produced a more specific financing complication. Bloomberg reported that additional due diligence had delayed progress on an upsized $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres, whose Malaysian facilities are said to serve ByteDance. The Financial Times separately reported that Nvidia told AI hardware manufacturers to stop shipping server computers to Southeast Asia as Washington tightened Chinese access to advanced chips. The Netherlands opposed proposed extraterritorial U.S. restrictions on ASML, saying they threatened the company. These developments place equipment access and end-user compliance directly beside financing execution.

In corporate developments, SAP is considering eliminating at least 10,000 positions, or at least 9% of its workforce, in an AI-focused restructuring. People familiar with the plan said numbers could change after labor negotiations; a German employment guarantee runs through 2028. Japan Tobacco and Altria are exploring a potential takeover of Imperial Brands, which said it would consider a proposal but had received no approach.

Banking transactions and regulation added separate capital questions. Dubai Islamic Bank announced an all-stock acquisition of Emirates Islamic that would create a group with about $159 billion of assets. It would issue 3.49 billion shares to Emirates NBD, with the target valued at approximately 31.1 billion dirhams, or $8.5 billion. UBS's leadership sought to reassure employees after a Swiss parliamentary committee supported a $16 billion increase in capital requirements. UniCredit plans to nominate Andrea Orcel as Commerzbank supervisory-board chairman and seek replacement of all 10 shareholder representatives after obtaining final regulatory approval for its takeover.

## Next Open-Session Watch

Friday's reopening will bring the gilt-futures decision into trading. ICE futures begin at 1 a.m. London time, ahead of the 8 a.m. cash opening, creating the first opportunity for investors to adjust positions built around the abandoned delivery-basket proposal. In credit, Vanke may circulate its extension terms more widely on Friday, while Trans-Oil's expected November 30 waiver remains a nearer financing deadline.

Middle East developments remain a risk to the energy assumptions underlying central-bank decisions. Houthi attacks targeted Saudi Red Sea ports, with minor damage and no civilian injuries reported at Jazan and a drone intercepted near Jeddah Islamic Port. An attack on a Saudi refinery also threatened exports. Iran's claim that vessels struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz lacked independent confirmation. The Saudi-led oil alliance was considering carrying current output quotas into January. Export disruption and the eventual production decision could alter the inflation outlook when bond markets reopen.

Spain's November 29 election presents a more contained sovereign test in Barclays economists' assessment, because a mainstream center-right or center-left party is likely to lead the government. Scope Ratings said the country's credit outlook remained supported by factors relatively independent of the electoral cycle. Corporate policy could change more visibly: the People's Party favors extending nuclear generation and removing a phased requirement for data centers to obtain 80% of hourly electricity needs from renewables. Those proposals would change the regulatory setting for utilities and power-intensive investment.

Canada's quarterly GDP and November employment releases next week precede the December 9 rate decision and will test the resilience assumed in the banks' newly unanimous hike forecasts. Philippine November inflation is due December 4, providing a direct check on the easing-price-pressure thesis behind expectations for further bond gains. The Federal Reserve's H.4.1 balance-sheet release, shifted from Thursday for Thanksgiving, is scheduled for Friday, November 27, at 4:30 p.m. New York time.

section_summaries.summary: The Thanksgiving closure left U.S. bonds without same-day price discovery. South Korea resumed tightening as the semiconductor boom drove stronger growth forecasts, while the ECB's October account revealed how widely officials had considered an immediate hike. European leaders also advanced the ECB succession by recommending Pablo Hernandez de Cos.

section_summaries.summary: South Korea raised its policy rate to 3.25% and signaled room for another increase, while ECB officials explained their gradual response to worsening inflation. The BOE considered gilt-repo haircuts, and ICE retained its existing gilt-futures delivery basket. Vanke discussed weaker upfront repayment terms and Trans-Oil awaited a covenant waiver, even as Ares arranged $1.3 billion for Cary Group's buyout. Ethiopia launched an $880 million bond exchange.

Friday's gilt reopening follows ICE's abandoned basket restriction, alongside possible circulation of Vanke's extension terms and Trans-Oil's November 30 waiver deadline. Middle East export risks could change central banks' energy assumptions. Canada's GDP and employment releases next week test unanimous bank forecasts for a December hike; Philippine inflation on December 4 tests expectations for further domestic bond gains.

methodology_note: SIFMA recommends a full U.S. fixed-income market close for Thanksgiving Day. No prior-session market levels are presented as current-day moves.

overall_summary.headline: South Korea raises rates as ECB deliberations underscore persistent inflation risks
overall_summary.session_narrative:
U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Thanksgiving Day, leaving no same-day U.S. bond price discovery. The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% and lifted growth forecasts to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027. Its median six-month rate projection rose to 3.5%. Semiconductor profits supported the stronger outlook, although their benefits had yet to spread strongly to household consumption; slower global AI investment remains a risk to further tightening.

The ECB's October account showed that many officials thought an immediate hike could have been justified. They chose a gradual response to the predominantly energy-driven shock, with no material second-round effects so far and earlier tightening transmitting through lending. EU leaders recommended Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next president, with the formal process expected to finish in December. The transition comes as persistent inflation and sovereign-debt strains challenge policy.

Britain's BOE considered minimum gilt-repo haircuts to constrain leverage. ICE separately abandoned a proposed gilt-futures delivery-basket restriction, opening scope for the relative cheapening of affected bonds to reverse when trading resumes. In credit, Vanke discussed extending 1.2 billion yuan of principal for three years with weaker upfront payments than previous deals, while Trans-Oil expected an uncertain covenant waiver by November 30. Ethiopia launched an exchange of its defaulted $1 billion bond into an $880 million security.

Friday's gilt reopening will provide the first trading response to ICE's decision. Middle East attacks and the Saudi-led oil alliance's pending production decision could alter the energy assumptions behind central-bank policy when bond markets reopen.
overall_summary.summary: The semiconductor boom drove a sharp upgrade to South Korea's growth outlook and pointed to further tightening, while the ECB's October account showed broad support for a hike tempered by a measured response to the energy shock.
